You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test 'readEntriesOfSize0' verifies behavior when reading 7z archive entries, particularly focusing on entries with size 0 (empty entries). The test expects that calling read() on entries named "2.txt" or "5.txt" returns -1 (EOF), while for others it should return actual bytes.

The bug report highlights that calling SevenZFile.read() on an empty SevenZArchiveEntry throws an IllegalStateException. From the snippet of SevenZFile.read(), it delegates to read from getCurrentStream().

The getCurrentStream() method throws IllegalStateException if deferredBlockStreams is empty (meaning no active stream to read from).

The key method is buildDecodingStream(), which sets up streams for the current entry. It gets the folderIndex from the stream map using currentEntryIndex. If folderIndex < 0 (likely empty entry), it clears deferredBlockStreams and returns without adding any stream for reading.

Hence, for empty files, buildDecodingStream() does not add any input stream to deferredBlockStreams.

Then, when read() is called on this entry, getCurrentStream() sees deferredBlockStreams.isEmpty() and throws IllegalStateException as there is no stream to read from.

Thus, the bug arises because empty entries result in no stream being present in deferredBlockStreams, but calls to read() are still made and are not handled gracefully.

The test expects a -1 return value (EOF) when reading from empty entries. However, due to absence of a stream, an exception is thrown instead.

To fix this, probably buildDecodingStream() or getCurrentStream() should handle empty entries by providing a zero-length input stream so that reads return EOF gracefully instead of throwing an exception.

This explains the bug in detail: empty entries cause deferredBlockStreams to be empty, leading to IllegalStateException on read().

Recent bug reports about other archive format stream errors are not directly relevant here since this is specific to empty 7z entries and their decoding streams. The behavior and broken assumption in buildDecodingStream() is the root cause.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test 'readEntriesOfSize0' fails because reading an empty 7z archive entry (with size 0) triggers an IllegalStateException. The SevenZFile.read() method calls getCurrentStream().read(), where getCurrentStream() throws IllegalStateException if the list deferredBlockStreams is empty. In buildDecodingStream(), when the current entry corresponds to an empty file (indicated by folderIndex < 0), deferredBlockStreams is cleared but no placeholder empty stream is added. Consequently, deferredBlockStreams remains empty, causing getCurrentStream() to throw IllegalStateException on read attempts. The test expects read() to return -1 (EOF) on empty entries, but due to missing a zero-length input stream for these entries, an exception is thrown instead. This mismatch causes the test failure. Hence, the root cause is the absence of a zero-length stream for empty entries in buildDecodingStream(), leading to no available stream for reading and thus an IllegalStateException.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
